It has princes. One of them is on this floor, in the body of a giant snake, on a leash.
Station ten on the tangle, reachable only by taking the switch that everything sensible avoids.
A gnomish dreadnought that is also a castle and also somebody’s home, floating over the air quadrant with the way down sitting inside it.
The ground-floor strip club of the Desperado Club, and by some distance the least exclusive of the three.
A cat put on a hat on the first floor. It is payable on the ninth.

entities.name: Agatha is an enemy to all of you

taglines.text: The mysterious one from the elder care facility, named on the ninth floor as an enemy to all of them.
Something the dungeon was built to contain gets out, and the man who did it does not survive it.
Shi Maria went into him and did not come out.

entities.name: A hundred and twenty thousand children

taglines.text: Lucia Mar is carrying them. Nobody has said what for.
The dungeon's own population declared itself on live galactic television.
A Nine-Tier Attack poison, and a note saying the Gate was essential to beating whatever carries it.
Strange faults on the tenth floor, and they are getting more frequent.
Borant's grip and the Syndicate's authority both start to give.
It says so itself, on stage, through somebody else's mouth.
Doctor Hu, and something the retired crawlers know that the current ones do not.
Every exit failing at once, worldwide, while a demon prince tries to cast his way home.

beats.headline: The Bahamas, with Brad
beats.text: Subject is in the Bahamas with her ex, a man called Brad, and she posted the photograph. Carl ended it by phone a few days before the Transformation, which, as timing goes, was impeccable. She is not on my stairs. Her cat is. Her family's breeding line is. Her shoes are, on his feet, and they are pink. That is the file. I have never had so little to say about anyone, and I resent it.

beats.headline: January 3rd, 2:23 in the morning
beats.text: I crack the window of my apartment in Seattle for a cigarette. That's it. That's the whole decision. Donut, who is my ex-girlfriend's show cat and not mine in any way I agreed to, goes out through it and up the tree, and I go after her into the freezing dark in my leather jacket, boxers and Bea's pink Crocs, with a Zippo and half a pack of Marlboro Reds. Mrs Parsons leans out to ask about the noise. Then every building on the planet comes down at once, and everyone who stayed inside one is gone.

beats.headline: The terms
beats.text: Reach the bottom and humanity gets Earth back. Nobody expects that to happen. The clock is the one rule the dungeon never bends, because the collapse is how a season is scheduled.

beats.headline: The first voice after the world ends
beats.text: One minute after the Transformation, I make my first announcement, planet-wide, to whoever is still standing. The dungeon has eighteen levels. Earth can be reclaimed from the Borant Corporation by conquering it. Then I put in the staircases. From here on, every rule, every notification and every insult you receive arrives in my voice. Get comfortable with it. I have.

beats.headline: January 3rd, and then the announcement
beats.text: It takes a minute. Then the System AI speaks planet-wide: the dungeon has eighteen levels, and the planet can be reclaimed from the Borant Corporation by conquering it. The staircases appear. The survivors are, near enough without exception, the people who happened to be standing outside — smokers, insomniacs, night-shift workers and anyone chasing a pet.

beats.headline: The foreclosure
beats.text: It claims Earth under Syndicate law and turns the surface into a mining claim. The dungeon is the legal cover and the revenue at once. Its guides work on indenture — Mordecai among them.

beats.headline: The way down is lit from below
beats.text: Every floor is joined to the next by one, and each floor sets its own terms for who may use it and when. They are generally well lit, and the warmth comes up rather than down, so a crawler standing at the top is being invited by something that has already decided what happens next.

beats.headline: Tutorial Guild Hall, first floor
beats.text: Rule one: I don't open the door until you kill a goblin. The cat desecrates my mother. The man blows up a Murder Dozer. I open the door. My name is Mordecai. Borant holds my indenture, which means I guide for the first three floors and run a magic guild after that, where they mostly leave me alone to brew and look up old friends. Try to live long enough for that to matter.

beats.headline: Ratings are currency
beats.text: Ratings buy sponsors, sponsors send gold and loot, and loot buys another floor. Being watchable is a survival stat, and production will alter the dungeon to get a better episode.

beats.headline: Law, tax and standing
beats.text: It licenses the crawl, taxes Borant per box tier and runs the courts. Which makes it the one institution here that can be argued with.

beats.headline: Thirteen million go down the stairs
beats.text: The tutorial gives Carl the count along with his HUD and menus.

beats.headline: She takes it out of his hand
beats.text: It comes out of the Legendary Pet Box awarded for being the first crawler to bring a cat down the stairs. She snatches it, melts into a heap of furry goo, and gets up talking.

beats.headline: Where they come from, and how they open
beats.text: Achievements, bosses (Boss Boxes, scaling with the boss's rank), quests, and viewers (Fan Boxes and Benefactor Boxes). They stay locked in the Awards and Boxes tab until a safe room or guildhall, and then it is all or nothing — every box you have opens in sequence, lowest tier first, and you cannot pick. Read every description before equipping anything. As Mordecai puts it: always, always, no exceptions.

beats.headline: The top tiers cost the house real money
beats.text: Borant owes the Syndicate tax on the tier of every non-sponsored box it hands out. In the whole history of the show only 2,145 Celestial boxes have ever been awarded, and no crawler has had more than four. The previous record for one season was eighteen, which bankrupted the Naga showrunners and kept them out of the business for centuries.

beats.headline: Benefactor Boxes ignore the theme
beats.text: Only patrons can send them, and they are the one kind that will produce a pulse rifle or powered armour in a fantasy dungeon. A Bronze Benefactor Box beats a plain Gold Adventurer Box.

beats.headline: Dressed for nothing, and stuck that way
beats.text: An hour past the stairs and I have a Goblin Pass Tattoo on my left forearm, a Trollskin Shirt of Pummeling, a Nightgaunt Cloak of Stoutness clipped to the jacket and a Toe Ring of the Splatter Skunk. What I do not have is shoes. I have asked. The dungeon has heard me ask, and the dungeon has an opinion about it.

beats.headline: First cat down the stairs
beats.text: Carl carries me down, and the dungeon gives him a Legendary Pet Box for it, which is fair, and gives me a Legendary Quadruped Box of my own, which is more than fair. His box has a biscuit in it. An Enhanced Pet Biscuit. I take it out of his hand, because it is obviously for me, and I melt into a heap of goo, and I get up talking. I have a great deal to say.

beats.headline: Named in the crown's warning
beats.text: Every royal in the line must kill the Sultan and every other member of the family before descending to the tenth floor.

beats.headline: Eight floors of fuse
beats.text: The Crown of the Sepsis Whore puts Donut in the Blood Sultanate's line of succession, and taking it off does not undo it.

beats.headline: Out of the Legendary Quadruped Box
beats.text: Awarded for being the first cat into the dungeon. A deep purple stone at the centre, clouded and swirling as though it were liquid. +5 Intelligence, +5 Good First Impression, and a 15% chance for any attack to inflict Sepsis. Donut puts it on without reading past the stats.

beats.headline: The part she skipped
beats.text: "Warning! (Seriously though. I'm going to say this again. WARNING! Read this shit before you put it on.) Placing this crown upon your head permanently places you within the royal line of succession for the Blood Sultanate on the ninth floor of the world dungeon. Removing this item will not remove this status. Royal members of the Blood Sultanate will be required to slay the Sultan and all other members of the royal family before descending to the tenth floor. You'll only want to wear this if you're a blood-thirsty, raging psychopath."

beats.headline: Bolts from the eyes of a Persian
beats.text: Bolts of energy leave the caster’s eyes one after another, and the resemblance to a film about spaceships is close enough that nobody bothers to pretend otherwise. Princess Donut works it out for herself once Mordecai has switched her menus on, and from that point the question is never whether she will fire, only at what.

beats.headline: GC BWR NW Princess Donut the Queen Anne Chonk
beats.text: I learn Magic Missile. I also have the highest stat total in the party, which makes me party leader, which anyone could have predicted. My first act is to give the party a proper name: the Royal Court of Princess Donut. There is an inauguration. Carl does not take it seriously enough, but there is an inauguration.

beats.headline: She equips a crown with an ominous description
beats.text: Mordecai says read the description first. Mordecai says a great many things. It is a crown, it is dark and smoky and exactly my colour, and it came out of my box, which has the word Legendary on it. It has a vulgar name, which is not my fault. It says something about the Blood Sultanate and a line of succession, eight floors down. I am already a princess. I do not see how being in line for anything could be a demotion. Carl is making his face.

beats.headline: Formally inaugurated
beats.text: Party leadership goes to the highest stat total. Her first act with it is to rename the party after herself. On a show, a name the audience will repeat is not a joke — it is an asset.

beats.headline: The protector behind the counter
beats.text: A stout dwarfish people, shaggy in both sexes, who mostly appear in the dungeon as non-combatant staff. They cook, they hand over what the room owes a crawler, and they are miserly about every part of it that is left to their discretion. The first one on the stairs runs a safe room and is called Tally.

beats.headline: Green on a map that is otherwise unlit
beats.text: They sit throughout the dungeon and they show green on the minimap even through fog, which makes them the only honest thing on it. Inside there are restrooms, somewhere to lie down, and three televisions showing the crawl to the people doing the crawl. Most are staffed. The staff are not there for the crawlers’ benefit.

beats.headline: Safe rooms are not safe
beats.text: Folks come down those stairs frightened, and frightened folks go looking for a door with the word safe on it. That is where you'll find them, sitting still, and that is where Maggie and I find them. The monsters on these first floors are hardly worth the trouble. A person is worth a good deal more. Production knows exactly what we are, and production puts us on the air every chance it gets. You draw your own conclusion about who the show is for.

beats.headline: The first episode airs
beats.text: The crawlers get to watch themselves. Borant patches the hallway bathroom bug in the same breath.

beats.headline: The face of the broadcast
beats.text: Subject hosts. He is orange-hued and four-eyed and built along lizard lines, and he delivers the rundown of each floor at a pace that does not permit anyone watching to think about what is being described. He also takes the live commentary on special events. I have worked with him for a long time and I have never heard him ask a question he did not already have the answer card for.

beats.headline: Seen in the first episode
beats.text: I'm on the show. The first episode of Dungeon Crawler World: Earth, and I'm in it, so everybody with a screen has seen me now, including a man with no shoes and his cat. I watched the whole thing. I didn't say anything while it was on. I liked it more than I thought I would.

beats.headline: Steam, two wheels and a seat for royalty
beats.text: Goblin-made, steam-driven, and assembled with an optimism the materials do not support. The sidecar is the part that matters: it is exactly the size of a cat who has recently decided she is a queen, and it settles the question of how the party is going to travel.

beats.headline: Entry is a tattoo
beats.text: Carl and Donut both take the Desperado Pass Tattoo in a first-floor safe room — his on the neck, hers on the right shoulder blade, glowing gold through the fur. Donut is appalled.

beats.headline: The mysterious Agatha
beats.text: Agatha. She is with the Meadow Lark party when Carl and Donut find them: Imani, Yolanda Martinez, the Andrews brothers, and her. The others I can account for, level by level, box by box, all the way back to the stairs. Agatha I can account for. Mostly. Let's leave it there. The party calls her mysterious, which is the kindest word available and also the most accurate.

beats.headline: The good folks from Meadow Lark
beats.text: We came down out of Meadow Lark, the elder care facility, together: Yolanda Martinez, the Andrews brothers, Brandon and Chris, me, and Agatha, who none of us can quite place and who came with us anyway. Carl and Donut find us, and we sit down and trade stories, theirs and ours, and then we make a plan, because there are people depending on us and a plan is what you owe them.

beats.headline: Imani, Yolanda, the Andrews brothers, and Agatha
beats.text: Carl and Donut find them on the first floor. Tales are exchanged, plans are formed, and the Royal Court agrees to keep helping them.

beats.headline: The manager who is on holiday
beats.text: Subject holds a manager’s contract for one of the teams and treats the posting as time off. She drinks. She smokes blitz sticks. She has, on one occasion, charmed a boss, which is more than most managers achieve and rather less than her team needs from her on any given afternoon. Her crawlers know exactly what they have been given.

beats.headline: The Ball of Swine
beats.text: Seven of us against the Ball of Swine: Brandon, Chris, Yolanda, Carl, Donut, Agatha and me, fighting from the redoubt. It is the first time this group has fought as one thing instead of six people and a cat standing near each other, and it works. Afterwards I count everybody twice, because that is what I do, and everybody is there both times.

beats.headline: Introduced on the third recap
beats.text: A whole faction enters the story as a broadcast segment.

beats.headline: The Ball of Swine
beats.text: Brandon, Chris, Yolanda, Imani, Carl, Donut and Agatha take it down out of the redoubt.

beats.headline: It introduces you to your rivals
beats.text: The third recap brings in Le Mouvement, and then a boss battle. Whole factions arrive in the story as segments.

beats.headline: She fights beside them, then takes her leave
beats.text: For the record: Agatha fought the Ball of Swine from the redoubt beside Brandon, Chris, Yolanda, Imani, Carl and the cat, and did her share. Then, in the aftermath, while everyone else was agreeing to keep helping Meadow Lark, she took her leave. No forwarding address. I nearly always have a forwarding address.

beats.headline: The production trailer
beats.text: Down the stairs, sideways, and out into a trailer that is not in the dungeon at all. Lexis is waiting: five and a half feet, thin the way her people are thin, blonde hair pinned tight, plain black dress, and a light musical voice that sounds like a cartoon. She walks them through how the tunnelling works and how the recording works in the fewest words that will do the job. Associate producer on a chat show, and also the first person from the far side of a camera either of them has met. The cat takes to it at once. The man starts trying the drawers.

beats.headline: Blocking out the segment
beats.text: She and the cat block out a segment of Dungeon Crawler After Hours while the man works his way round the room testing what is nailed down. All of it is nailed down. He gets nothing. Lexis notices, and says nothing about it, which is the whole of her professional personality in one gesture. Then Odette arrives and the trailer stops being about anybody else.

beats.headline: What it costs when it stops working
beats.text: A guide explains his own body by naming the race he picked in his own crawl. He can no longer shift at will, so the dungeon assigns him a shape at the start of every floor and he wears what he is given, always something that belongs on that floor. The race is a gift with a clause, and he is the clause.

beats.headline: He has done this before, and it cost him everything
beats.text: I crawled. I took Changeling, and I can't shift on my own any more, so the dungeon hands me a body at the start of every floor and I wear what I'm given. This one is a rat-kin. What I actually am is golden, and has wings. I don't talk about the family. When I've had enough to drink, I talk about the family.

beats.headline: Loot is only semi-random
beats.text: About the boxes. Sometimes what's inside is random. Sometimes I choose it, by hand, because a crawler needs helping or hurting and the numbers want a show. You will never know which, and that is the point. I also hand out insults on purpose. Carl has a Bronze Asshole's Box and a Gold Asshole's Box, both earned on this floor for killing non-combatants. I named them. I'm proud of them. He is not.

beats.headline: Every body on the floor makes more of them
beats.text: Each corpse produced on this floor spawns between one and fifteen, and they keep coming until five thousand of them hold a quadrant. Destroying the bodies stops the grubs growing stronger; it does not stop them arriving. The floor is therefore a choice between leaving your dead where they fall and feeding the thing that eats them.

beats.headline: Carl gets her inside
beats.text: The next episode is tunnelling through and I am not, at my age, built for sprinting. Carl, the young man with the cat, takes hold of me and hauls me into the safe room like a sack of feed, and I let him, because I am old and not stupid. Then the ceiling announces Rage Elementals. Of course it does. The day was missing a garnish.

beats.headline: The bathroom rule
beats.text: An announcement goes out between episodes. Any human-born crawler who relieves themselves outside a designated bathroom area gets one summoned on the spot, and it will take the offender and every crawler in their party with them. It is not an encounter. It is a penalty, dragged up from a floor nobody on this one is meant to see.

beats.headline: Named in a drunken confession
beats.text: Crawler Princess Donut, under the Buzzed debuff from a blended corpse, informs Crawler Carl that she loves him. Almost as much as Bea. Almost as much as Ferdinand. Ferdinand is the other cat. That is the whole entry: a cat, ranked above the man who carried her down the stairs, by a cat. I keep records on everything in this dungeon. This one I opened for the ranking.

beats.headline: The thing behind the moonshine
beats.text: Twenty feet of immobile octopus in a chamber with Live, Laugh, Love spelled out over the door in cut wooden letters, sitting behind a still that produces toilet-grade moonshine at industrial volume. Her tentacles are lined with human mouths that scream without pause and drip something that stops a body healing. The cat and the barefoot man take her apart and drink a blended corpse to do it. She is not the point. She is a copy, and somewhere there is an original, and the original is a committee.

beats.headline: There are other shows
beats.text: Zev explains crawler participation on Syndicate programmes. Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem, Shadow Boxer, Vengeance of the Daughter, the Blood Hunter — a crawler can be signed to any of them, and the contracts do not lapse between floors.

beats.headline: She explains how the shows work
beats.text: Okay. So. Carl has just met his first Borant dungeon admin and managed to be civil, which I am counting as a win for everyone, including me. My job today is to walk them through how crawlers take part in the Syndicate programmes, and I get through all of it. Then Princess Donut mentions Gossip Girl, and Mordecai has seen it, and I have seen it, and for a few minutes nobody in the room is anyone's liaison.

beats.headline: Nothing to fight
beats.text: One arrives in the residential blocks. Arrows pass through the smoke without raising a health bar at all, and a magic missile raises a flicker of one that it heals straight off. Gravity reverses. Yolanda goes down covering Randall, and Imani, Chris and Brandon get the rest of the residents behind a safe room door while Carl pulls Elle in.

beats.headline: It hammers on the door for hours
beats.text: The survivors sit through the recap while it rages outside. The thing does not tire and it does not wander off. Fire is the one lever: a jug of boom takes a quarter of it away and the burn holds the healing back afterwards. The rules change the same day, so that no crawler can sit in a safe room until the collapse.

beats.headline: One man and his ex-girlfriend's cat
beats.text: Carl finishes the Bomb Chicken and takes it out with everyone in the universe watching. Bombs, obstacles, a safe room door used as an ejector, and one exploit the designers never priced in. The elemental is no more.

beats.headline: Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem
beats.text: The Maestro puts Zhang and me up against Brindled Vespas and does all the talking for us. That is the show. We are the part that gets hurt. Then Carl, the one with the cat, works out that he is worth too much to the production to be punished, and gambles on it, in front of everyone, and it holds. He gets us out. Zhang, our boss, me, and my sister Li Na. I owe a man I have just met more than I have ever owed anyone.

beats.headline: Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem
beats.text: The show is Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem. The host calls himself the Maestro. He pulls my brother and Zhang off the floor and makes them play a guessing game for points that buy lives, and they will not choose which of us to spend them on. The rest of us stay frozen where we were standing, between the troglodytes and the Brindled Vespas. Then the crawler with the cat, Carl, decides he is too valuable to the production to be punished, and bets on it, out loud, and the four of us walk out. I am remembering his face.

beats.headline: Glurp, glurp
beats.text: Two crawlers, Li Jun and Zhang, a pack of Brindled Vespas, and me with the microphone. That is the format. The format works, and I am very, very good at it. Then the one with the cat opens his mouth. He wagers, on my air, that the production will not dare touch him, and the production, to my everlasting disgust, does not. He walks the whole group off my show alive. Every one of them. Glurp, glurp. We will be right back.

beats.headline: Two teleport points, four people
beats.text: Li Jun and I are standing on a stage in front of the Maestro while he plays with us, and behind us Li Na and the manager are boxed in between hatching Brindled Vespas and troglodytes with nowhere to go. We have two teleport points. Two. I say put them on Li Jun and Li Na and leave me where I am, because that is the arithmetic and somebody has to say it out loud. Then a barefoot man starts whispering, and the arithmetic changes.

beats.headline: Find Crawler
beats.text: Carl's trap closes on Yvette, and her own mother finishes what the trap started. What Maggie My walks out of it holding is a Legendary Skill Potion of Find Crawler. There is exactly one crawler she wants found.

beats.headline: The girl who would not kill anything
beats.text: Yvette. Level one, which at this depth is not an accident and is not luck. Her guide told her what every guide tells them, which is that the fastest way up is other people, and she declined. Her mother and father did not decline. Eight so far by my count, all of them sitting quietly in rooms with the word safe written on the door. The daughter walked behind her parents the whole way down. She has killed nothing at all.

beats.headline: Her mother's hands
beats.text: Crawler Yvette is dead. Her father lifted a lit stick of dynamite out of a rat's corpse in a corridor the barefoot man had been through, and the blast took her rather than him. Nothing anyone poured into her did the slightest good. Her mother understood that faster than anybody else in the room, and put her hands around her daughter's throat, and afterwards a box dropped containing a Legendary Skill Potion of Find Crawler. I am obliged to announce the drop. I am not obliged to say anything about the rest of it, and I find that I would rather not.

beats.headline: Under a million
beats.text: A recap, a wipe of Le Mouvement, and the remaining-crawler count drops below seven figures. Carl hears that number the way other people hear a tap dripping.

beats.headline: Wiped
beats.text: Another recap carries the news, and the remaining-crawler count drops below a million in the same broadcast.

beats.headline: Seven inches of pink feathers, in a cage
beats.text: CAGE. Small. Pink? Pink. TWO BIG THINGS. Bite them. Bite them. Bite. MOTHER. Mother has grubs. Grubs open. Inside part GOOD. Mongo stays.

beats.headline: She adopts a dinosaur
beats.text: There is a reward room on the second floor with a cage in it, and in the cage is a pet-class mob, and the pet-class mob is my son. I did not know that until I saw him. He is called Mongo. He is mine, and that is the end of the discussion.

beats.headline: The footwear situation does not improve
beats.text: The second floor finally addresses my feet. It hands me an Enchanted Pedicure Kit of the Sylph. So now I am still barefoot, but my feet are shiny and they glitter, and the audience has noticed, and the audience does not let things go.

beats.headline: Taken with the Cat race
beats.text: Her constitution rules out melee, so she fights on charisma and spells. The per-level pick is why a show cat out-scales most of the humans, and Mordecai points out she keeps the skills from every class she leaves behind.

beats.headline: Manoeuvred into managing a cat
beats.text: Odette says my memory is the most valuable thing a crawler could get hold of, so the two of them arrange for me to become the cat's manager during class selection, and they make it look like an accident. It was not an accident. I will forgive Donut. Carl, no.

beats.headline: Her advice makes the party
beats.text: The Princess took my advice, which is what advice is for. A class that lets her choose another every time she levels, and a manager who has walked those floors himself and remembers every one of them. Mordecai is not to know he was steered. He would sulk, he would be entitled to, and a sulking guide is no use to anybody. Some gifts are best received as accidents. I have given a great many that way.

beats.headline: Cat, and a Former Child Actor
beats.text: Odette suggested it, so obviously it is a good idea: a class that lets me choose another class at every level. I also arrange for Mordecai to be my manager. He is thrilled. He does not show it, but he is. My constitution is apparently far too low for what Carl calls melee, so I will be fighting with charisma, spells and the audience, which is how it should be done.

beats.headline: Primal, and a Compensated Anarchist
beats.text: Class selection, on the way into the Over City. I take Primal for the race and a monk-rogue hybrid nobody has picked before, and the AI writes me up as "a trapmaking, bomb-making, social-media dynamo" who "will happily throw a Molotov through a window one moment and step in front of a camera to plead for the violence to stop the next." I'd argue with it if I could think of the argument.

beats.headline: Taken with the Primal race
beats.text: "Will happily throw a Molotov through a window one moment and step in front of a camera to plead for the violence to stop the next."

beats.headline: Carl takes the empty box
beats.text: Race selection, on the way into the Over City. The preview model for this one is blank, because nobody alive knows what they looked like. Mordecai's summary: the progenitors, the first species to conquer the universe, the boogeymen of the cosmos, gone one day without a note. Taking it costs five stat points against staying human. What it buys is a ceiling. Every skill trainable to twenty, where most crawlers get one or two past fifteen in a whole crawl.

beats.headline: Three of something there was one of
beats.text: Cast on a pet or a minion, the target appears to split into three. The duplicates look right and act independently, and the System does not mark which one it started with. It arrives in a box on the Over City, in the same delivery as a cat tree and a scented candle, which is roughly the level of seriousness the dungeon brings to its gifts.

beats.headline: The circus in the Over City
beats.text: Grimaldi's Traveling Circus is pitched in one of the Over City's districts. Ringmaster Redstone Grimaldi, proprietor. Tonight two crawlers, Carl and Princess Donut, are scouting the grounds as the mobs form up for the night. That is the whole entry so far: a tent, a company, and two people looking at it from the dark. Filed under Over City, third floor.

beats.headline: Met outside Grimaldi's circus
beats.text: Night comes down on the Over City and the mobs form their lines around Grimaldi's Traveling Circus. Two crawlers have come to scout it, a man and a cat, and they leave under magical mortar fire, and I am what they run into on the other side. My charisma stands past a hundred. He stares, as they all stare. Then he snaps his own finger, and it breaks. I have not decided whether to be offended.

beats.headline: The rules he cannot break
beats.text: Most of what I know I'm not allowed to volunteer. Some of it I can only give you if you ask the exact question. Without press credentials nobody watching can see me or hear me, and as a manager I can't touch a mob. My advice is what it has always been: stay ahead of the curve, never trust an elite, stay away from gods. Carl has heard all three.

beats.headline: Carl signs on to her show
beats.text: Grimaldi has lifted my banishment. Carl went into his head to ask him, and I asked with him. I may leave the circus behind me at last and go where my vengeance waits, and that is the sixth floor, not here. Carl has agreed to be part of it as well, the Vengeance of the Daughter, when it comes to its proper act. Before he went in he sat and read a spellbook. Wisp Armor. It guards the mind against control, and he wanted it on him before he swallowed the worms that let Grimaldi speak inside his skull. He does not walk into another creature's mind unarmoured. Nor would I.

beats.headline: Carl signs on
beats.text: He makes a deal to appear on the programme when it moves to the sixth floor. Before giving his word he reads a Wisp Armor spellbook for cover against mind control, then buys an ice cream cone of parasitic worms from Apollon the Mighty so he can speak inside Grimaldi's head and talk him into lifting Signet's banishment.

beats.headline: He stands over her
beats.text: Mother down. Mother NOT MOVING. Mongo on top of Mother. Spiky things. MANY spiky things. Bite. Bite. Bite. Hurts. Mongo stays on Mother. Carl says something. Mongo does not listen to Carl.

beats.headline: Acute Ears, in a safe room
beats.text: Donut drinks one and comes up with Acute Ears, plus fang caps for Mongo. Carl comes out of the same haul with a great deal of explosive and a Scroll of Upgrade that improves his boxers, which is roughly the ratio he has come to expect.

beats.headline: A goat on the recap
beats.text: Subject is a goat. Specifically a Boer goat, bonded as a dungeon familiar, and she appears on the recap in the same segment that introduces the crawler she belongs to. The audience takes to her immediately, which is a thing the audience does with goats and which production has learned to plan around.

beats.headline: First time on the recap
beats.text: They ran me on the recap tonight. Miriam, Pony and Bianca too, first time for all four of us, I'm told. I don't know what they showed. I wasn't doing anything I would call footage. Ifechi and I keep moving and keep our heads down, and I would have preferred to stay a name nobody had learned yet. Too late for that.

beats.headline: On the door of the Desperado Club
beats.text: Subject is a Crocodilian, an intelligent, thick-skinned, semi-aquatic people who are not celebrated for their quickness, and she works the door of the club. This is a non-combatant posting, which describes her contract rather than her capabilities. Nobody has yet found the argument that gets past her.

beats.headline: A starter kit for three bottles of moonshine
beats.text: Mordecai comes through my door with a barefoot human and a talking cat, which is the sort of shift I am having, and I have not seen the man in years. He wants a starter kit for the human. I want the three bottles of Rev-Up sitting in the human's inventory, because the stuff is filth and filth sells. Kit, a Hair of the Dog, and we call it square. Being a manager is a sweet gig, friend. Nobody upstairs breathing down my back.

beats.headline: What he says about the girl with the dogs
beats.text: Word of advice with the kit, no charge. There was a girl in here last night. Small one. Lucia Mar. She let her dogs off the leash on my floor and made a mess of my evening, so she is barred, and I do not care what the audience out there thinks of her. If she comes anywhere near you, remember that a place like this one bars almost nobody.

beats.headline: Voted in by an audience
beats.text: The first fan boxes come open in the Over City. Donut draws a framed photograph of Bea and Brad. Carl draws a xistera: a wicker scoop two feet long that straps to his hand and arm and hurls whatever he pulls out of his inventory into it, adjusting itself around the shape of the thing. He had been trying to make a slingshot work. The fans had watched him do it.

beats.headline: A name on a dead boss
beats.text: There is a level seventeen neighbourhood boss in an abandoned swimming pool, and there is nothing alive in the water any more. I did that on my own. My family came down with me, twenty of us, and the Over City took all of them inside a week. So I hunt, and the kill notice carries my name and nothing else, which is accurate.

beats.headline: You are not seeing the magistrate
beats.text: Two of them at my desk. A human with no shoes, a cat that talks, and a body. They have put a body on my desk. Evidence, they call it, and they have a note for it, so the swordsmen leave without him. The magistrate is not to be disturbed. If he does not care about your business then he will certainly care about being disturbed, and I will not be discussing it further. Behind me is a shelf of Jaxbrin figures in their proper order, and the human is standing far too close to it. The door behind me is locked. It is locked for a reason.

beats.headline: A seat on the Danger Zone panel
beats.text: Ripper Wonton's panel, and the crawler and his cat are on it. I keep reaching for his hand and my claws keep going straight through his fingers, which does not stop me reaching. Then the Skull Empire fire at those two and hit Manasa instead. My friend. The comedian starts treating her death as a piece of political arithmetic, and I tell him to shut his mouth. The Prism Kingdom condemns the action, and I say so on air within the hour: we will bring a grievance against the Skull Empire in the Syndicate Courts.

beats.headline: The statement read out on air
beats.text: Subject is the crown prince, brother to the Maestro, a coarse-haired boar-like creature with lean muscle and a manner that is meant to be read as cruelty and largely succeeds. When his empire fires on a trailer and takes someone who was nobody’s enemy, it is his statement that goes out on air. He does not write it and he does not disown it.

beats.headline: Danger Zone, with two new guests
beats.text: Welcome back, folks. On the panel tonight: Evo, Princess D'nadia, Manasa, Butler, Hekla, and the two everybody in this galaxy has been waiting to get in a chair. Tucker takes most of the questions, which is how we do things here, and when the cat takes Tucker apart on air I laugh out loud, because it was funny and because he had it coming. Then the barefoot one starts talking about revolution inside the Skull Empire, and I let him talk, because a guest of mine gets to finish a sentence.

beats.headline: The show goes dark
beats.text: And then the Skull Empire answers my guest by firing on the trailer next door, and they take Manasa, who was on my panel and was nobody's enemy and was not even the target. We go off air while I find out what happened. Then we come back and I read Prince Stalwart's statement out on air, because that is the job, and then I say what I think of it, because that is also the job. By the time I finish saying it the Valtay have taken his yacht apart with his family aboard, and folks, none of this is entertainment any more.

beats.headline: Carl plants a seed on Danger Zone
beats.text: Two sentences of provocation on a chat show, and the Skull Empire answers them. It kills Manasa, which was a mistake, and the Valtay answer that in turn by destroying Prince Stalwart's yacht with his mother and the Maestro aboard. Nobody in the studio raises their voice. Three funerals come of it anyway.

beats.headline: He closes with Manasa singing
beats.text: We are out of time and I am not doing a comedy sting tonight. Roll the tape of Manasa singing. All of it. Hold on her through the credits and do not cut away for the sponsor. Goodnight, folks.

beats.headline: They carry her as far as they can
beats.text: A neighbourhood boss and a borough boss with Katia and Eva in tow, until class selection splits everyone up and the levels stop adding up.

beats.headline: She goes on without her
beats.text: Katia and I came in together. Same profession, same door into this place. Class selection separated us; that is what it does, it separates people. I kept moving. I did not stand in a corridor waiting for someone who was not ready to be there. Call it what you like. I call it the difference between the people who are still here and the people who are not.

beats.headline: She asks them to take her
beats.text: We carried Katia and Eva through a neighbourhood boss and a borough boss, and I would do it again. Then class selection split us, and I run this party on numbers, and Katia's numbers stopped adding up next to anyone she stands beside. I cannot carry that down another set of stairs. So I am the one asking. Carl. Donut. Take her. She is better than she looks right now, and she will hate that I said so.

beats.headline: The recap makes the introduction
beats.text: The recap does the introductions this dungeon never bothers with. Florin is partied with Ifechi now, and the two of them are moving up the board fast enough that I have opened a file. She was a medic on Earth, which down here is a class and a liability at the same time, since the one thing nobody in this place will let you do is keep other people alive. Note it and move on. The audience already has.

beats.headline: Ten levels behind and nobody's problem
beats.text: I came in with Eva. We fell in with Hekla and Brynhild's Daughters, who carried the two of us through a neighbourhood boss and a borough boss, and I know exactly how much of that was us. Class selection split us up, and Eva did not wait. Now Hekla is asking Carl and Donut to take me. The system has just upgraded my displayed race from "What the f-word?" to "Human", so things are looking up.

beats.headline: Doppelgänger, Monster Truck Driver
beats.text: Bannon, my guide, talked me into it: a momentum-based constitution tank who can reshape her own mass, body and equipped gear together, into any form of the same weight. I sculpted my face using my reflection in a health potion bottle. Carl says it looks like a Juan Gris. He is being kind, and I would know.

beats.headline: Out for their blood
beats.text: The recap showed it, so now everybody knows. I'm looking for the cat and the man. Princess Donut and Carl. Not everybody in the city. Them. I know their names and I know what they look like and I know they are on this floor. I'm not going to tell you why. You don't need to know why.

beats.headline: Dynamite in the shelves
beats.text: They came back in the night. Into my building, into my office, and they put hobgoblin dynamite in among my figures, which is the one place nobody ever looks, because nobody but me has ever cared what stands on that shelf. I did not hear them. Nobody comes into this building at night. It has never once happened in all the years I have kept this desk.

beats.headline: The administrative building, and everything in it
beats.text: Miss Quill is dead. The administrative building came apart with her inside it, along with what was left of Magistrate Featherfall, who was bones long before any of this, and the shelf, and every figure on it. The barefoot man is magistrate of this settlement now, which is what happens when nobody checks the paperwork. He collects one achievement for assassinating a public official and a second for spoiling a Tigran's quest, since Bautista had been coming for her himself. She kept that door for a very long time and not one crawler ever thought to ask her why.

beats.headline: A survivor gives up his name
beats.text: A woman called Burgundy has been pulled alive out of a nest of Krasue in the ruin of my old building, and she has given two crawlers my name and told them where I am kept. Miss Quill's undead husband, she called me. Accurate, as far as it goes, and it does not go far. Nobody has had cause to say my name aloud in a very long time. I know what that means. I have known what it would mean since the day I was pulled back.

beats.headline: He thanks the two who took his revenge
beats.text: Five of them went in seconds, to Former Circus Lemurs, in a street I could not reach. The cousin who ran out with me gave up the next day. Now I climb out of the rubble to find the lemurs already dead by somebody else's hand, and the secretary I had a quest to kill dead by the same hand, and none of it mine. So I swear a debt to a cat and a man with no shoes, give them my chat contact, and point them at a stairwell three kilometres east. Then I ask the man the question I cannot answer for myself: how can we make it to heaven if God does not recognise us?

beats.headline: They take him for a lich
beats.text: They come across the floor towards me with the cat out in front and a fuse somewhere behind, and they have decided that I am a lich, that I am the borough boss, and that finishing me finishes their quest. I am no lich. I am no boss. I am a level one bird with no feathers left and a hole in the world where my back used to be, and if they lay a hand on me their souls come out through the scratch and go into the tank, and I have no way on this earth to give them back.

beats.headline: She spends a death sentence saving NPCs
beats.text: The Fools Who Broke the Glass quest is close to unsurvivable, and it triggers before I have earned my place. I spend the time getting NPCs out. I tell Carl and Donut to save themselves. I mean it.

beats.headline: Correction to the file
beats.text: Remex tells them the rest of it, there being nobody left to stop him. She was not guarding the magistrate. She was guarding what she had done to her own husband: dragged him back into the world as a soul leech, bound to her permanently, and installed under the town to drink its soul crystal dry so that she would have the mana for a working called The Final War. The devotion to the figures was real. The refusals at that desk were real. Both of them were also the cover, and I filed her as an obstructive minor official for the whole of the season.

beats.headline: Soul Leech Capacitor
beats.text: You asked before you detonated anything, which is more than most would do, so here is the story. A Soul Leech Capacitor is what a necromancer builds when what they want is a battery with a face. The spell reaches for the soul the target loved best and drags that soul back into the world, tied to them for good. My wife cast for me. Since then I have been drinking this town's soul crystal dry, and she has been spending what I collect, and what she is spending it on is a working called The Final War. I agreed to none of it. I would like that written down somewhere.

beats.headline: Built in the middle of a collapse
beats.text: During the Fools Who Broke the Glass, Carl drops a Sheol Glass Reaper Case around a Soul Crystal that is already going up and pulls the result into his inventory. Rated Pretty Damn Rare. Status: Explosion Imminent. "This item can no longer be stabilized."

beats.headline: Forty-five kilometres
beats.text: Enough to take a city and every suburb around it. He cannot drop it, sell it or make it safe, and it detonates the millisecond it is out of his hands. "Created by a man who murders babies and steals rare collectibles from his elders."

beats.headline: Destroying it does not help
beats.text: The crown is blown apart in the Over City's collapse. The succession survives it.

beats.headline: Destroyed, and it changes nothing
beats.text: The third blast of the Over City's collapse takes the crown apart. The succession is untouched. It said as much on the label.

beats.headline: Four shocks, and a town coming apart
beats.text: Remex is finished. He began to convulse and the settlement went with him: a foreshock that stripped the enchantments off every piece of gear in the district, a second that set weapons off where they hung, a third that took the Enchanted Crown of the Sepsis Whore apart, and a fourth that reached into every crawler's hotlist and triggered all of it at once. Ranger Conrad E detonated where he stood. Katia dropped the Swordsmen Depot. For the record: he asked them not to come closer, he explained precisely why, and he was the most honest thing in that town.

beats.headline: A part in a bomb
beats.text: The word arrives the way most of the dungeon's cosmology does: buried in an item description. A Sheol Glass Reaper Case is half of what makes an explosion large enough to rattle the teeth of a god. Nothing explains where the glass comes from, and nobody asks.

beats.headline: It burns a veto rather than pay
beats.text: Eighty-three Celestial boxes are owed. Borant voids them with its one seasonal veto and is still liable for the one that was already open, which lands it in front of a Syndicate court. A production company that cheap has seams worth looking for.

beats.headline: Eighty-three Celestials, and one veto
beats.text: A quest reward gets double-upgraded to Celestial for 83 crawlers. Borant burns its single seasonal veto to void them and is a moment too slow — Quan Ch has already opened his, which leaves the company liable and in a Syndicate court. The upgrade achievements responsible are patched out immediately.

beats.headline: He opens his before the veto lands
beats.text: Eighty-three crawlers are owed Celestial boxes at the close of this floor. Borant appeals the ruling and loses, appeals the prizes and loses again, and then burns its one seasonal veto here, voiding the lot. It is a fraction too slow. Crawler Quan Ch's box is already open, and you cannot un-open a Celestial box, not even with a veto. So the count comes to one: a level fifteen trooper in a glowing robe that lifts him off the ground. The veto was not mine. I want that on record.

beats.headline: The cliff at the fourth floor
beats.text: The early floors are built to bury crawlers in low-tier loot and beginner skills. From here boxes and achievements get very much harder to come by.

beats.headline: They are waiting when the doors open
beats.text: The commonest ghoul on the line, and by the System’s own account the most tractable of them, which says more about the others than it does about these. They come at the court in the first minutes on the new floor, before anyone has established what the rules of the place are.

beats.headline: A level-5 space, from an odd little box
beats.text: Carl, Donut and Katia each get a special achievement whose box holds personal space coupons — beds, a shower, a crafting studio and a training room. Donut installs a cat tree.

beats.headline: One of the handful the show follows
beats.text: Two hours of highlights and she is in them: Elle, Team Li Na, Ifechi, Florin, Hekla, Prepotente, and the girl who is hunting the cat. That is the running order of this season, whatever the leaderboard prints. Being in the running order is not the same as being safe in it. It is nearer the opposite, and every one of them has worked that out by now.

beats.headline: On the recap
beats.text: They have put me on their recap, the programme between floors, in a row with humans. The captions say Elle, Li Na's team, Ifechi, Florin, Hekla, Lucia. And Miriam, of course, since she is the one who walked me into this place. I did not ask for the camera and I do not smile for it. If the audience wants a goat that performs, the audience can wait until I feel like singing, and then it can sit very still and listen.

beats.headline: The board, two hours in
beats.text: Elle, Team Li Na, Ifechi, Florin, Miriam, Prepotente, Hekla and Lucia, all in one broadcast. It is how the crawl keeps track of itself.

beats.headline: The Prize Carousel
beats.text: Crawlers, welcome to the Prize Carousel! Our contestant's fan box lit up the wheel, and when the wheel lights up, folks, that means me! And a twist before we even start: your guide is in time-out. Seven days, Mordecai, nothing personal, put your feet up. Now, to the prizes! Carl looks them over and picks... a book. A book, folks! Let's hear it for a man who knows exactly what he wants!

beats.headline: The prize for being watched
beats.text: Awarded for gathering a following, or for doing something in front of enough people that the following gathers itself. The contents are put to an audience vote, and the box will not open for thirty hours, so the crawler carries it around knowing that strangers are arguing about what they deserve.

beats.headline: Hired at the bar
beats.text: Transaction logged at the Desperado Club. Clients: Crawler Carl and Crawler Princess Donut. Hired: Bomo, mercenary, and the Sledge, mercenary, sold as a set. Also present at the bar, at no charge: Elle and Imani. The cat orders a dirty Shirley, in a bowl, with extra cherries, and gets it, because the Desperado knows who tips. Bomo's transcript is short. That is a feature, crawler. The talking ones cost more.

beats.headline: The twenty-fifth holder of the Cookbook
beats.text: Twenty-four crawlers carried this before me. Different seasons, different species, worlds that aren't there any more. Whatever I do from here, I'm finishing somebody else's work, and most of them never got to finish theirs.

beats.headline: The Tangle cannot be beaten alone
beats.text: The trains only come apart if hundreds of crawlers move at once, and getting hundreds of crawlers to do anything at once is exactly the thing production spends its money preventing. So I stop thinking of the explosives as the weapon.

beats.headline: A Cretin in evening dress
beats.text: Subject is a Cretin, seven feet of rock-coloured muscle, employed as a bodyguard on the club floor and dressed for it. He is not conversational. He is assigned where the club decides he is needed, and the arrangement has never yet required anyone to explain to him what the job involves.

beats.headline: Hiring, and a dirty Shirley
beats.text: They take on Bomo and the Sledge there and meet Elle and Imani. It stops being a bar the moment it becomes a labour market.

beats.headline: Introduced in the Iron Tangle
beats.text: It arrives with the sponsor tab unlocking. Twenty-four crawlers carried it first, across seasons and species, on worlds that lost. Rosetta Thagra, who turns up hosting Shadow Boxer, is one of the authors.

beats.headline: A name in the front of the book
beats.text: My name is in the Cookbook. That is the whole of what anyone here knows about me, and for a long while it was the whole of what I wanted them to know. Twenty-four of us wrote into it before this season, on worlds that mostly lost. You do not put your name on a thing like that expecting to be asked about it afterwards.

beats.headline: Bought at the bar
beats.text: Two crawlers come up to the counter and buy security. Me and Bomo, sold as the pair. That is the arrangement in this place. You pay, and we stand between you and whatever comes through the door. The cat is not what I expect. She orders a dirty Shirley in a bowl with extra cherries, drinks the whole thing, and then she wants dancing, so I do my version of the robot while she bops and twirls on my shoulders. Princess Donut. She calls me Sledgey. I let her.

beats.headline: The management apologises
beats.text: Astrid. Bloodlust Sprite, level 125, Cardiovascular Mage, assistant manager of the Desperado Club. The Bloodlust Sprite is one of the rarest and deadliest things her kind produces, born holding magic over anything with a circulatory system, and the signature trick is a heart beating fast enough to catch fire. She is the size of your hand, she wears a tuxedo, her hair is up in a bun, and her voice is deeper than yours. A crawler makes an attempt on Princess Donut on club grounds and Astrid comes down to say sorry in person. The Royal Court walks out with permanent complimentary security. Establishments like this one do not hand out refunds. She handed one out.

beats.headline: A miss on his own shift
beats.text: A crawler goes for the Princess on my floor, on my shift, and I do not get there in time. Elle puts the second one down. Astrid comes to apologise in person, and I stand where I am and wait to hear what a miss like that costs a body like me. Carl does not ask for blood. He asks for me and Bomo, permanent and complimentary, the Royal Court's own security every time they walk in. So now I have a court.

beats.headline: One at every fifth station
beats.text: Elle passes the word down the line: on this floor, every fifth station holds one. Same beak, same screaming mouths, repeated along the rails like an advertisement nobody can switch off. The dungeon does not run short of them, because running short is not a thing this creature can do. Take one apart and the original makes two.

beats.headline: A summoning barely avoided
beats.text: Gore-Gore, engineer, gives the party two routes back to the stairwell stations and then attacks them, which is the sequence I have come to expect from railway staff. In the middle of it he tries to bring in Grull. It does not land. Understand what almost happened there: a mob with a grudge and a prayer nearly put a war god into a train carriage with four crawlers. Horses pray to Grull. Centaurs pray to Grull. There are a great many horses on this floor.

beats.headline: Dismember, on the trains
beats.text: In the aftermath on the rails, Donut casts Hole and takes the head off a war mage called Dismember. Nobody stops to explain what one of those is, and there is a train to catch.

beats.headline: Stoking the Nightmare Express
beats.text: Subject is a Lesser Demon and a non-combatant, level seventy-five, and she shovels for the Nightmare Express. Where one finds large ovens that want feeding, one regularly finds her sort, and the tangle has more large ovens than it has anything else. She is on the crew that the crawlers need and does not pretend otherwise.

beats.headline: The switch nobody is meant to take
beats.text: The named trains run their loops until they reach a set of three switches, and only one of them leads here. Getting to it means reading the network rather than riding it, and the souvenir hats turn out to be the key to the whole arrangement, which is the sort of joke the fourth floor keeps making.

beats.headline: Boards at Trainyard E, off at station 60
beats.text: Subject is a level ten human and a non-combatant, filed as a Human Resources Associate for the line. She boards the Nightmare Express at Trainyard E and leaves it at station sixty, every time, which is the whole of her recorded behaviour. Her name was probably something else before the dungeon decided what a human resources associate should be called.

beats.headline: Whatever they are, they are at station 435
beats.text: A few dozen of them work directly under the line’s management, and they are stationed where the employees leave the train. Whether they count as a boss or as scenery depends entirely on who is describing them, which is a distinction the dungeon is happy to leave unsettled for as long as it is useful.

beats.headline: A curse, handed over at the Desperado Club
beats.text: Frank Q gives it to Carl at the Desperado Club, and it is meant as a curse. He and Maggie My made their daughter Yvette wear one to level up, and Yvette marked Carl in a safe room on the first floor. A wearer cannot heal while a mark lives, so when Yvette was hurt, Maggie had to kill her own daughter. Carl keeps the ring for the five percent.

beats.headline: Why nothing could be done for her
beats.text: Frank Q hands the barefoot man a ring at the club and calls it a gift, and the gift is the answer to a thing that man has been carrying since the second floor. The ring marks a target for death, and while the mark draws breath the wearer cannot be healed by any means at all. They put it on their daughter to bring her level up. She marked somebody in a safe room on the first floor and that somebody walked out of the room alive. So when the dynamite found her there was nothing on this planet that would have saved her, and her mother knew it before anyone else did, and did the only thing that was left. Maggie My is the most dangerous person on this world and here is the reason why.

beats.headline: A thousand crawlers stranded at 101
beats.text: A thousand of them are stuck at 101 on the Vermillion line, Li Jun's team among them, and there is a train sitting at 60. So I take my party into the Royal Court's safe room and I ask for help, which is not a thing I enjoy doing twice in one crawl. Katia means to use her own body as the plough. I let her offer it. That is the arithmetic.

beats.headline: A thousand stranded at 101
beats.text: We are stuck at 101 on the Vermillion line, my team and something like a thousand other crawlers, and we are not getting out on our own. Word comes through that Hekla's people have reached Carl's safe room and asked for his help, that a train is ready at stop 60, and that Katia means to use her own body to get it through. I do not know what that means. I have decided to find it encouraging.

beats.headline: Given memories of a child that was never made
beats.text: Subject conducts the Mango Line. He was also issued with a set of memories containing a daughter, and the daughter was never made, and he has not been told. He is found on the ground with his head down and a puddle forming underneath him. The memories work. That is the part of the design I would draw attention to.

beats.headline: Killed by the crawler she handed off
beats.text: Crawler Hekla is dead, on the train, in front of everyone. Her healer had orders to let Katia bleed, the idea being that Carl would swing first and give her a reason to put him down and the cat no choice about joining her. Then Katia aimed a Rush at Eva, went wide, and put Hekla against the wall of the cab instead. Golden Player Killer Skull. Five hundred thousand gold on Katia's head. Brynhild's Daughters do not survive the trip back.

beats.headline: She has her pick, and she uses it
beats.text: Subject works Communications for the Borant Corporation. As a Kua-Tin of the ruling ultra-nationalist party she takes preferential treatment as a matter of course, including first choice of which crawlers she handles. Brynhild’s Daughters were hers, and Hekla with them, and she has never once had to ask for an account she wanted.

beats.headline: The bartender who cannot go outside
beats.text: The ghouls came through station seventy-five. Everyone out on the platform died screaming while I stood behind my own bar and watched, because I cannot cross that doorway. Not will not. Cannot. Then a small woman walked in, put me down, took my alcohol and went on her way, and I woke up on my own floor stone cold sober, which is the worst part of the whole business. Good stock, good rag, no way to help anybody. If you tell me that is not cowardice I will believe you for about an hour.

beats.headline: Fourteen left hands
beats.text: Two carts to a line, two gnoll left hands to a cart, and there is exactly one gnoll in this station. Katia cannot shape a hand the cart will accept. I cannot walk out to the carts. What I can do is die and get up again, so that is the arrangement we come to, and Mongo does the work. First time, I came round sober and confused. After that I tried to fight him. After that I got in the corner and stayed there. Fourteen times, for four hundred crawlers stranded at the end of a line I will never see. Carl came and told me why. He did not have to.

beats.headline: The sixth hand on the cookbook
beats.text: Subject carried the cookbook and added to it, and several of her entries are rants rather than instructions. She came from a clawed race with annual migration patterns and lived on an island with her family before the stairs. The rants were left in. Everyone who has carried the book since has read them.

beats.headline: The Jaxbrin babies
beats.text: Jaxbrin Amusements sponsors me, and what they pay me in is children. Small stitched figures I can pour out of a case into a fight until nobody can count them. Miss Quill kept more than a thousand of the things in her apartment and never once knew what they were for. I have told Carl about them because he asked, and because a man who trades in explosives should know exactly what is about to come around the corner beside him.

beats.headline: The recap cuts it for laughs
beats.text: The last recap of the floor runs the whole thing with me being put down over and over and not one second of the reason for it. No rescue. No six hundred people stuck at the end of the line with no hats. No carts. Just a barefoot man doing that to a bartender, fourteen times, cut to music. I would like the record to show that I said yes.

beats.headline: The truer translation
beats.text: Mordecai puts a name to the thing the Iron Tangle keeps caricaturing. Apothecary is the closer translation, taken from what she can synthesise out of whatever she eats, and the dungeon's version bends the joke into an insult. She is a collective mind and she is spreading, which is a sentence that makes a great many people elsewhere nervous.

beats.headline: Bought for the housekeeping
beats.text: A personal space upgrade, available from the fourth floor at twenty-five thousand gold, sold on the promise that it will clean up after you. The units are capable of a good deal more than the sales copy admits, and the party buys one and puts it aside without yet knowing what they have bought.

beats.headline: Mordecai sees it on his hand
beats.text: Back from his suspension for throwing a chair at Chaco, Mordecai sees the ring on Carl's finger and tells him to get rid of it at once. Carl is wearing it for the five percent to all stats and nothing else, and keeps wearing it.

beats.headline: The tunnelling system
beats.text: Mordecai catches the team up on the shape of the wider universe, and two powers come out of it: the Apothecary, and the Plenty. The Plenty built the tunnelling system a few hundred seasons ago and kept it proprietary. Before it, most of the universe got the crawl on a delay of anything from an hour to a year. Prosperity, in other words, is a thing they sell.

beats.headline: The stairwell stations flood
beats.text: One day left on the floor clock and they come out of the deep tunnels in numbers nobody in production budgeted for. Thousands of them, growing as they travel, pouring into the stairwell stations while the surviving crawlers are still trying to get down. Carl warned everybody this was coming, in detail, on an open channel. Being right about it helps nobody at all.

beats.headline: A name nobody on the crawl can pronounce
beats.text: Subject is from Earth, born and raised in a small village in Mongolia, and took the Crisper Class. Her fellow crawlers gave up on her name inside a day and settled on a syllable of it. She takes constant needling from a certain cat about her race, and she fights beside that cat’s court regardless, which is a distinction the needling never quite grasps.

beats.headline: Still human, and heavier for it
beats.text: I stayed human at selection. No fur, no beak, nothing added on. Earth Mover for the class, which is a spellcaster and a wall in the same body, and Dirt Clod is exactly what it sounds like and it works better than it has any right to. The armour I am in now is black and gold and glows in the dark. Li Na says that is showing off. Li Na is not wrong.

beats.headline: Same plan, other side of the Tangle
beats.text: We worked it out some time ago: the ghouls keep coming while the generators stand, so the generators have to go, every one of them. We have been taking them from this side of the knot, Prepotente and I, at his pace, which is patient. He puts debuffs on a thing for hours and waits for it to fall. Now Carl's group arrives from the far side with the same plan, and they have just dropped into the abyss the boss my boy was two hours from finishing. He threatens them for it. I take my staff to the top of his head until he apologises, and I tell them all that two groups landing on the same plan only means the plan is good.

beats.headline: Grull against the Mimic Rex
beats.text: Crawler Carl, a Mimic Rex, and War God Grull, in one place, and the god is being driven by the Maestro like a stolen vehicle. Grull kills the mimic. Grull steps on Carl. Carl's friends come for him anyway, which is the part I did not have odds on, and by the finish Grull has been sent to the Abyss. Four storeys of war god, removed from the floor by people who were, this morning, worried about a train.

beats.headline: What the file says about him
beats.text: The file, for those keeping one. Grull is one of the few trueborn heirs to the Celestial Ascendency, which makes him a candidate for the throne of heaven, and level 250, which makes him unkillable on this floor. His worshippers are horses, centaurs and tikbalangs, and from this floor down the llama-shaped ones join in as well. They paint themselves blue and talk without stopping about wenches and dying gloriously in battle. Crawler Carl's guide gave the blunt summary of the whole subject a long way back: there are no real gods down here, only the ones who pay for the privilege.

beats.headline: Down into the bubble
beats.text: Carl, Donut and Katia come down into a sealed quadrant of their own and walk to the only town in it. Mordecai meets them there wearing a Skyfowl, which is what this floor has made of him. Donut takes the Glass Cannon class on the way in.

beats.headline: The orphan with the Walkman
beats.text: Subject is a changeling child of Hump Town, orphaned, and suffering compression sickness: in her default form she has no arms and her head is sunken. She owns a Walkman. The dungeon did not issue it to her and has not taken it away, and I am not going to be the one to file the paperwork that does.

beats.headline: A starter species, seeded on purpose
beats.text: The Syndicate keeps a handful of basic species for salting worlds it intends to use, and this is one of them. They are proud enough that most who reach class selection keep the race rather than trade it, which is a decision the dungeon is content to reward and to punish in the same breath. Mordecai wears the shape on the fifth floor.

beats.headline: What is in the town hall
beats.text: Skarn lends Carl his telescope for a look out at the Wasteland, and explains why the gnomes riding it leave this town and the Bactrian village alone. It is not mercy. It is what both places keep in their town halls.

beats.headline: He runs the telescope
beats.text: Subject is a juvenile changeling, roughly eight, orphaned when the gnomes bombed his town, and now living in Hump Town under the care of an adult who took the job without being asked. He operates the telescope. He is good at it, and he is the reason anyone in that town knows what is coming before it arrives.

beats.headline: The castle is the aircraft
beats.text: The flying home of the dirigible gnomes and a heavily armed military platform, and there is no seam between the two. It holds the air quadrant of the bubble, and the stairs down sit inside it, which settles what anyone wanting to leave the floor is going to have to do about it.

beats.headline: The desert quadrant
beats.text: Crawler Firas. Fifth floor, desert quadrant. Located in the company of Crawler Louis and Langley's team, a party of car salesmen who have taken up the bow, at the moment Crawler Carl's group came looking for other crawlers. Keeps close to Louis. Present for the march on the Bactrian town and for the run back to Hump Town that followed it. The file on this one is thin. So is the file on most of you.

beats.headline: Regroup
beats.text: The party goes out looking for other crawlers in the quadrant and finds Firas, Louis, and Langley's team of car salesmen who have taken up the bow. A Thorny Devil and a Gnomish Drop Bear turn the whole march back short of the Bactrian town, so everybody comes back here instead.

beats.headline: A team of car salesmen with bows
beats.text: Subject leads a six-man team of archers, all of whom sold cars in Finland and all of whom picked the Archer Class together, which is either loyalty or a failure of imagination and has worked out the same either way. They come into the fifth floor as strangers to the court and do not stay strangers.

beats.headline: The desert quadrant
beats.text: Okay so, me and Firas are out in the desert with Langley's guys, who are, no joke, car salesmen. With bows. Pretty good with the bows. Then Carl's crew comes over the dune looking for other crawlers, and, hey, found some. We all head for the Bactrian town together, and a Thorny Devil and a Gnomish Drop Bear have thoughts about that, so we head back to Hump Town instead. Not a loss, man. A regroup.

beats.headline: Florin's own bullets, turned around
beats.text: Crawler Ifechi is dead. The recap of the previous floor carried it in full: Lucia Mar reflected Florin's bullets back along the line they came from, and Ifechi was standing behind them. A Red Cross medic, top ten, the best thing that had happened to Florin since the stairs. He watched it, and then he watched it again on the recap with everybody else, which is a detail I did not write into the format and cannot take out of it.

beats.headline: Debuff stacking, ruined
beats.text: Watch the highlights from the last floor, since they insist on replaying them. Miriam and I are stacking debuffs onto a boss, one on top of the other, timed to the second, the way it is supposed to be done and the way nobody else in this dungeon can do it. Then Quan Ch walks into the middle of it, and the plan is gone. The best work I have done in this place, and that is the part they replay.

beats.headline: He wrecks the debuff stack
beats.text: Recap, highlights from the previous floor. Crawler Miriam Dom and Crawler Prepotente working a boss down the careful way: stack the debuffs, keep the rhythm, let the arithmetic do the killing. It is good technique and it films well. Then Crawler Quan Ch gets involved, and it comes apart. I am not going to editorialise. The footage editorialises for me.

beats.headline: Built on the floor it is meant to cross
beats.text: Assembled by hand out of what the fifth floor makes available, which is not much and none of it intended for the purpose. It moves, it carries the court, and the System files a description of it that reads as an insult and functions as an advertisement.

beats.headline: Louis brings her
beats.text: Louis found me and Louis brought me, because he is sweet and because I asked. Now the other crawlers in the quadrant have found Carl's group, and Carl's group has a cat who talks. Their manager, Mordecai, is sobering Louis and Firas up on the spot. All the fun is coming out of their blood at once. Louis looks very sad about it. I am not sad. I am here, and I am staying.

beats.headline: The tomb raiders, so called
beats.text: Subject kept the Human race and took the rogue-type Spy Class, and earned his way into the club on that. His party holds the subterranean quadrant of their bubble. Carl calls them the tomb raiders, which is not their name for themselves and is the one that stuck.

beats.headline: The guards are not what they look like
beats.text: In the town hall basement, some of the Dromedarian guards are changelings wearing the uniform, and one of their own has been torturing a prisoner to make him give up flesh. A race that can be anyone is a race that can be planted anywhere, and both sides of this floor have worked that out.

beats.headline: The basement under the town hall
beats.text: Hump Town's town hall, and a good number of the Dromedarian guards are not Dromedarians. In the basement is Wynne, held as collateral, and Wynne is willing to say who has been working on him. Henrik. Principal of the town, changeling underneath, level 50. What he wants out of Wynne is a spell that will put flesh on Quetzalcoatlus, and the method for getting it has been to take Wynne apart slowly enough that he might change his mind. Crawlers from the subterranean quadrant appear at the boundary and put Wynne down before any of it concludes.

beats.headline: A name out of a basement
beats.text: The name surfaces in a cellar under Hump Town, out of a man being taken apart in pieces. Wynne is being worked on to give up a spell, and the spell is meant to put flesh on Quetzalcoatlus. Whatever she is, she is worth a body to somebody, and somebody is prepared to do that to a man over several days in order to get her one.

beats.headline: Carl's second sponsor
beats.text: Donut is taken by Veriluxx RealPet Companions and Katia by the Squim Conglomerate, and neither of those needs explaining: a pet brand wants the cat, a conglomerate wants the coverage. Carl is taken by the Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network, which is registered as a not-for-conquest, answers to no system government and pays no tax. Nobody can say what it wants.

beats.headline: One root vegetable
beats.text: The Valtay Corporation sends a neural enhancer, which is exactly the sort of thing a corporation sends. The Network sends a single Toraline root vegetable. Mordecai has never seen the plant, cannot price it against anything, and cannot say what it is for. The box it arrived in cost more than the gift.

beats.headline: A creditor with a seat at the table
beats.text: A corporate system government inside the Syndicate, which is to say a company that is also a country and answers to neither description when it is inconvenient. Its people are parasites in the literal sense, riding the bodies of other races. It holds the Borant Corporation’s debt, and it sends a crawler a neural enhancer, which is the sort of gift that is also a note.

beats.headline: Hidden in the tomb
beats.text: Carl learns of it from the description of Ruckus, out in the desert quadrant. It lies buried in the Necropolis of Anser, and it has drawn treasure hunters for decades: the bugbear submarine captain Shamus Chaindrive, who spent close to twenty years looking for the tomb, a colony of dirigible gnomes, and the Mad Dune Mage. An artifact of this grade has no business appearing before the eighth or ninth floor, and the AI times out repeatedly reconciling the conflict.

beats.headline: Three pieces, three holders
beats.text: A winding box and two magically linked pocket watches. Henrik the Changeling has one watch, the gnomish Commandant Kane the other, and Ghazi the box. The quest to collect all three offers a reward of "Oh boy-oh-boy."

beats.headline: The bubbles are inhabited
beats.text: The pocket worlds are not stage sets. A bubble holds Hump Town and its changelings on the sand, a castle of dirigible gnomes in the air, the Necropolis of Anser underneath, and every one of them was there and running before a crawler arrived.

beats.headline: He explains the collateral
beats.text: Carl and Princess Donut sit down with Henrik and he explains how collateral works here, which is the local economy in miniature: a body held against a promise, and the promise enforced by what may be done to the body. He is patient about it. He answers every question put to him. Then the tomb starts taking on water and the conversation is over.

beats.headline: The delegation to the gnomes
beats.text: The plan walks out of the hall in a line: Carl, Princess Donut, Firas, Louis, Katia Grim out of sight, a reanimated Wynne, and Henrik. They meet Leon, the Gnome Negotiator, and present Wynne as a man in urgent need of healing. Princess Donut offers to do the healing in exchange for passage onto the Wasteland. Leon will take three of them and no more: Wynne, the cat, and Carl. The rest of the delegation, changeling included, is left standing on the sand.

beats.headline: The bombs never land
beats.text: Carl, Donut and Katia get aboard the Vahana and take it in mid-air with Langley's team shooting from the ground. Carl puts rounds into the Wasteland's bombs before they can be dropped on the town. The Wasteland breaks apart and comes down. The castle it carried stays up.

beats.headline: Bronze from a sponsor beats gold from the floor
beats.text: Only a sponsor can send one. They use the same six quality tiers as every other box and they outclass the ordinary run of loot at every rank, so a bronze one from a benefactor is worth more than a gold one earned. It means the fastest way to be well equipped is to be liked by someone with money.

beats.headline: A Scree riding Chris Andrews
beats.text: Frank Q is dead. Chris Andrews killed him, and Chris Andrews was not the one driving. Maggie My is back in the dungeon as a Scree, riding inside another crawler, and Frank died of exactly the thing he brought down here with him. He spoke to Carl one last time at the Desperado Club and called what was coming a gift. This was the gift. Half of a pair who taught this planet what safe rooms are for. The other half is still walking around, wearing somebody else.

beats.headline: Why the changelings want her flesh
beats.text: Juice Box lays out the arithmetic. The changelings want Quetzalcoatlus given a body so that they can touch her, because touching a thing is how a changeling adds it to the shapes it can wear. And they need what she carries: a great many of them are sick with compression sickness, and they believe she has a spell that alters living things which can be turned on the illness. A wailing shrieker over a tomb, wanted for her hands and for her medicine.

beats.headline: She brings them inside
beats.text: Subject is a juvenile Dirigible Gnome of the air quadrant, daughter of a commandant.
